lines: In the village of the tomb builders, Paneb had painted the walls of kings for forty years.
But now, his eyes were failing.
He told no one. Not even his daughter, Meret.
But she saw how his lines had begun to shake.
So every night, while he slept, she came down to the workshop...
and copied his figures, line by line, until her hand moved exactly like his.
And every morning, before he woke, she climbed to the tomb, and finished his wall for him.
One day, the master of the works came to Paneb's door.
He said his painting had never been finer. And Paneb understood.
That evening, he found her at the wall, and took her hands in his.

lines.say: I wondered whose hands these were.
They were always going to be yours.

lines: Some things we pass on with words.
The best ones... we pass on with our hands.
